🎙 Pakistani FM spokesperson calls for media cooperation with Iran to counter fake news

📌 Islamabad, IRNA — The spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Pakistan has emphasized the importance of bilateral engagement with the Islamic Republic of Iran, calling for strengthening media cooperation between the two nations to counter fake news and fabricated narratives.

Sajjad Haider Khan was speaking to reporters following a meeting with his Iranian counterpart, Esmaeil Baqaei, on the sidelines of the 30th Meeting of the Council of Ministers of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) in Islamabad on Monday.
​
Describing his discussions with the Iranian diplomat, who is accompanying Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi at the ECO summit, as “constructive,” Khan revealed that Baqaei, during the meeting, extended an invitation for him to visit Tehran later this month, which the Pakistani official hailed as a positive, forward-looking approach.
​
He also underscored the strong, friendly, fraternal ties between the two countries and pointed to Islamabad’s role in fostering regional peace, particularly in the wake of the joint US-Israeli war of aggression on Iran.
​
The Pakistani Foreign Ministry spokesperson said that both sides have agreed on the necessity of establishing regional peace and stability, affirming his country’s commitment to continuing its constructive role toward this objective.
​
In response to a question from an IRNA correspondent, Khan, while appreciating the active presence of Iranian media in Pakistan, including during weekly press briefings at the Foreign Ministry, called for media cooperation to counter fake news and fabricated narratives, which he said pose a serious challenge.

⚡️ Another violating tanker catches fire east of Strait of Hormuz: Iran Navy

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Another tanker violating maritime regulations caught fire early Monday after striking a naval mine in a prohibited area east of the Strait of Hormuz, the Iranian Navy says.

The vessel was immobilized following the incident, which occurred in the early hours of the day, the Navy said in a statement.
​
It said it maintained intelligence surveillance and continuous control over vessel traffic east of the strategic waterway.
​
The Navy warned that vessels switching off tracking systems or entering prohibited and unsafe maritime zones without authorization faced serious risks.
​
It added that owners of vessels disregarding warnings and regulations would be responsible for the consequences.
​
In a separate statement hours earlier, the Iranian Navy said an oil tanker caught fire after violating regulations and striking a sea mine in the eastern part of the Strait of Hormuz.
​
The Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) also said in a statement that two more oil tankers burst into flames after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
​
Iran closed off the Strait of Hormuz in response to the US violations of an Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) that was expected to end the war of aggression on Iran.
